stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( f(1) = 4 \), \( f(3) = 5 \), \( f(9) = -2 \). Let \( g(x) = \int_{x^{2}}^{10} f(t) \, dt \). Find the value of \( g'\left(3\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Reversing the limits, \( g(x) = -\int_{10}^{x^{2}} f(t) \, dt \), so by the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus its derivative is minus the integrand evaluated at \( x^{2} \).
The chain rule multiplies by the derivative of \( x^{2} \), which is \( 2 x \).
At \( x = 3 \) the limit is \( 9 \) and its derivative is \( 6 \).

parameter_draw.form: composite limit in the lower position

difficulty_variables.upper limit equal to x versus a function: composite limit in the lower position

distractor_derivations.A: -f(9) with the factor u'(3) = 6 left off
distractor_derivations.B: integrand evaluated at x = 3 instead of at the limit 9
distractor_derivations.C: sign of the reversed limits lost, as if the variable limit were the upper limit
